text:
maria: Quick FYI — starting a small experiment this morning to bias the autoscaler toward steady-state. Goal: reduce burst churn and tail latency by preferring reserved capacity up to a weighted factor before allowing burst. want quick eyes on the config and rollback plan.

raj: Can you summarize the tuning change in 1 line and the safety nets?

maria: 1) Introduce a 'reserved_weight' param that multiplies reserved capacity when computing desired replicas. 2) Keep current burst_budget but add a per-cluster burst_slope limit to prevent immediate large swings. Safety: canary to 5% of traffic, auto-rollback if p95 latency > 100ms over baseline or if preemptible GPU evictions spike > 2x.

dylan: Ran a 6h sim on last week's load. Key numbers: steady-state GPU hours down 12%, burst invocations down 18%, p50 unchanged, p95 improved ~6ms. Cost delta projected -9% for the canary fleet. attaching quick chart: https://files.redwood/test/oversub-chart.png

anya: Nice. What's the exact config we push? paste below?

maria: Pushing this to canary; config snippet: ```json
{"autoscaler": "multi-tier", "reserved_weight": 1.35, "burst_budget": 120, "burst_slope_limit": 0.15, "evaluation_window_s": 60, "rollback_conditions": ["p95_latency > 100ms","evictions_rate > 2x"]}
```

leo: 2 quick asks: 1) cost center tagging for any new nodes spun up during canary? 2) what's expected GPU-hours delta on a 24h run so finance can flag it.

maria: 1) yes — canary nodes tagged with cost_center=autoscale-expt. 2) extrapolated from sim: ~-10% GPU-hours on typical weekday. I'll DM finance the projection numbers.

raj: How are we routing traffic to canary? region split or percentage?

maria: Percentage split global: start 0.5% -> 2% -> 5% over 30m increments if no rollback tripped. If any condition hits, we cut to 0% and notify.

dylan: Added a short runbook note in the PR: 
- monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency (prod route), queue length, evictions_per_min, batch_size distribution
- alert threshold: p95 > 100ms for 3 consecutive eval windows OR evictions_per_min > 0.05
- rollback: flip canary weight to 0 and revert config in infra repo

maria: Also enabling verbose sampling for a subset of requests to check KV cache hit-rate impact. will post logs to /s3/autoscale-expts/1915551111/ .

leo: Good. If we see fewer bursts but sustained higher baseline cost, we need a kill switch. Make sure ops-runbook-bot is subscribed.

sre-bot: INCIDENT BOT: Canary rollout scheduled by maria at 2026-03-18T09:12Z. Auto-rollback conditions registered. Subscribers: eng-infra, oncall.

anya: one more question — how does this interact with quota-based region fallback? if EU is constrained and we prefer reserved, do we risk routing more to us-west and hitting network egress?

maria: good point — policy respects region affinity. reserved_weight is computed per-region. fallback still applies when headroom < threshold; we won't shift cross-region just because of weight. I'll add an explicit test for region-locality in canary checks.

raj: Thanks. One last ask: capture the sim command you ran so others can reproduce.

dylan: `./sim-run -trace recent-week.json -policy weighted_res -weight 1.35 -burst_budget 120 -out sim-1915551111.csv`

maria: Ok rolling at 09:15. Will post canary metrics after first 30m. Ping me if you want access to the dashboard (i'll share link). :rocket:
